text: Agent, thanks for getting here on short notice.
We have a situation at Viral Dynamics Media. ENTROPY's Social Fabric cell is operating there.
Three weeks ago, we flagged suspicious activity at Viral Dynamics—far beyond typical disinformation work.
Our intel suggests they're coordinating something larger. Data collection, psychological profiling, attack infrastructure.
The details are unclear, but it's active and operational.
Large-scale data aggregation. Personal profiles, vulnerability assessments.
Whatever they're building, it's targeted and sophisticated.
Your job is to get inside and find out what they're actually planning.
Derek Lawson. Senior Marketing Manager at Viral Dynamics.
He's been there about eighteen months. The timeline matches when the suspicious activity started.
He's ENTROPY, but we don't know the full scope of what he's running.
You're going in as an IT contractor hired to audit their network security.
Completely legitimate. Viral Dynamics actually requested the audit weeks ago. We just... made sure we got the contract.
Server room, computers, network infrastructure—all fair game under your cover.
That's where you'll find evidence of what Derek's planning. Look for encrypted files, attack infrastructure, target databases.
One more thing: there's someone inside named Maya Chen.
She contacted us anonymously. Suspected something was wrong but doesn't have the full picture.
Find her. She might have critical information. And protect her identity—if Derek finds out she tipped us off, she's in danger.
You'll have phone comms with me throughout. I'll provide guidance as needed.
There's a SAFETYNET drop-site terminal in their server room for submitting intercepted intelligence.
Everything you need looks like standard IT equipment. Stay in character. The IT department can provide you with a Kali Linux terminal, and lockpicks.
And document everything you find. We need complete evidence of whatever they're planning.
Remember—Derek doesn't know we're onto him. This is just a routine IT audit as far as he's concerned.
Use that advantage. Gather intelligence and evidence before making any moves.
The IT manager—Kevin Park—is your entry point. Build rapport with him.
He's not ENTROPY, just overworked and underpaid. He'll appreciate competent help and give you access.
Sarah O'Brien is the receptionist. Professional, friendly. Don't give her any reason to flag you.
And Maya Chen—the analyst who contacted us. Be careful around her. Derek might be watching who she talks to.
Get inside, find out what ENTROPY is planning, and report back.
Talk to Maya. She's your best lead. Whatever Derek's building, she'll have seen pieces of it.
Once you know what we're dealing with, contact me. We'll figure out how to stop it.
Viral Dynamics Media. A weekday morning in the city centre.
Eight floors of glass, and a mural over the door that somebody was paid a lot for. Staff drift in with coffee and lanyards.
It went through. Not on an open line. Come back to HQ.
A SAFETYNET operations room. Director Netherton is already on his feet; Agent HaX is patching in the technical desk.
Agent 0x00. ENTROPY used to steal. Now they break the things people can't live without.
I want my best in the room and my best on the wire. Nightshade has read the control systems. HaX has the rest.
The physics doesn't lie and neither do I. If they reach the safety interlocks, this stops being a hack and starts being a body count.
Get me a real reading off that floor, and I'll tell you how much time we actually have.
HaX. Go.
A grid battery site, and ENTROPY are inside it.
Worse than Ransomware Incorporated. This lot don't want paying.
Albion Energy Storage. Two hundred megawatt-hours of grid batteries.
A cell called Critical Mass got in as maintenance contractors, under the name OptiGrid Solutions.
They own the SCADA network now, the control system that runs the battery racks.
Two hundred and forty thousand people get their power through that site.
Lithium cells are safe while they stay under their charge limit and their cooling holds.
Critical Mass have bypassed the safety interlocks on all three rack banks and faked the temperature sensors. An overcharge trigger is armed.
If it fires, the cells heat past the point where they can stop themselves, and they catch.
One rack lights the next, then the hydrogen goes. The hall burns and the grid drops.
Yes.
ENTROPY's infrastructure cell. Power storage, generation, transport.
They answer to Blackout: Dr James Mercer. He signs the casualty models, and he has never once revised one down.
Mercer won't be on site. His lieutenant runs Albion, calls himself Voltage. Former grid engineer, which is why he got this one.
Don't go in hoping to talk him round. He knows exactly what happens to the night crew. He's costed them.
Ask. Quickly.
Their traffic puts it at eight in the morning, local time.
That's your window. It's tight, and they're ready for interference.
Three operatives on site: Cipher, Relay and Static. And Voltage.
Yes. More of them than you've faced before, and none of them amateurs.
Cipher holds Battery Hall 1. Relay walks the inverter room. Static stays with Voltage in the plant room.
You don't have to fight all of them. Your cover and that cloner will get you past more than your fists will. If they make you, you're cleared to.
Whatever force it takes to stop that trigger. But I want Voltage breathing. He knows things.
That's the order.
You're the grid-safety regulator Albion is expecting today. Four hours early.
Credentials are in your kit. Find Robert Vance. He runs the site, and he's on shift. He isn't expecting anyone before dawn.
He doesn't know about ENTROPY. The cover gets you in.
Your call. Vance is a career engineer, safety first, and he knows that plant.
Tell him and he'll help. Nobody on site knows those control systems better.
But if they're watching him, your cover goes with his.
Read him first. Hard evidence will do the persuading for you.
Good.
The Zero Day job left us one line. "Zero Day supplies, Critical Mass executes. Grid storage, this winter."
Well, it's winter, and this is the site.
Social Fabric are standing by to amplify the panic. Strikes across the region, all timed for eight o'clock.
One mind behind it, the one the directive named: The Architect. Voltage answers up that chain. Take him, and we're closer to whoever's setting the clock on all of it.
The same one. Stop it, take Voltage if you can, and bring out anything that names the next target.
So. Get in on the regulator cover and find Vance.
Then prove how they took the control network. Their jump server's in the engineering workshop. Whatever you pull off it goes into the drop-site terminal.
The plant room has a hardwired Emergency Shutdown button, the ESD. No network path, so it's the one control they couldn't take.
Press it and the banks isolate, once grid control believes you. They'll believe Nightshade, if you get a real reading off those racks.
And the operatives. Voltage alive, if you can.
Kit: your picks, the cloner from the WhiteHat job, and a laptop with CyberChef on it. No PIN cracker. We have one, it's ENTROPY's, and it isn't leaving the lab.
Go carefully. They've had three days to get ready for you.
The site's twenty minutes out. The gate will want your credentials.
Show them the regulator badge. You're a routine audit that came early.
If it comes to a fight, keep your head.
Good luck. Find Vance first.
The guard looks up from the desk and gets to his feet.
Morning. Bit early for visitors. Desk first, if you don't mind.
He turns your badge over, glances at the clipboard, hands it back.
Regulator, is it.
Alright, sign in here. Mr Vance said there was an audit today. He's not happy about it, fair warning.
Go on through, my lover. Operations office is straight down the hall.
Past the gate it's forensics' site, not ours. Anything you want, take it now.
Voltage's operation log is still on the plant-room bench, for one.
And there's a go-bag at the dock nobody's opened.
Fine. The banks will keep.
Forensics are almost on-site. Last chance.
Voltage's operation log is still on the plant-room bench, for one.
And there's a go-bag at the dock nobody's opened.
Loading dock. The van with no livery.
Forensics are almost on-site. Last chance.
Voltage's operation log is still on the plant-room bench, for one.
And there's a go-bag at the dock nobody's opened.
Loading dock. The van with no livery.
Albion's grid is someone else's problem now.
Agent, report.
